# FreeRTOS Timer and Task Subsystem

TinyBFT runs on a single FreeRTOS event loop (`tbft_replica_run`) backed
by a small set of `esp_timer`-based interval timers. Heavy cryptographic
work never executes inside a timer callback — the timers only set
event bits, and the replica task performs the real work.

## Overview

The replica uses four conceptual timers (`vtimer`, `stimer`, `rtimer`,
`ntimer`) but only the first two are actually allocated. All four are
declared in `tbft_replica_t` (`src/tbft_replica.h:102-104`); the latter
two are placeholders for future recovery and keep-alive logic. The
allocated timers are wrapped in a small `tbft_itimer_t` abstraction
backed by `esp_timer`.

## tbft_itimer_t (esp_timer wrapper)

Defined at `src/tbft_itimer.h:21-27`:

```c
typedef struct {
    esp_timer_handle_t  handle;
    tbft_timer_cb_t     cb;
    void               *arg;
    volatile bool       running;
    int64_t             period_us;   /* last-started timeout */
} tbft_itimer_t;
```

| Field | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `handle` | Opaque `esp_timer` handle returned by `esp_timer_create` |
| `cb` | User callback invoked from the dispatcher |
| `arg` | Opaque argument passed to `cb` |
| `running` | `true` while the one-shot is scheduled. Volatile for cross-task visibility |
| `period_us` | The most recently started timeout, in microseconds |

The public API (`src/tbft_itimer.h:37-60`):

| Function | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `tbft_itimer_init(t, cb, arg, name)` | Create the underlying `esp_timer`. The timer is *not* started. |
| `tbft_itimer_start(t, timeout_us)` | (Re)start as a one-shot. Always calls `esp_timer_stop` first to avoid races (`src/tbft_itimer.c:46-61`). |
| `tbft_itimer_stop(t)` | Idempotent stop. Sets `running = false`. |
| `tbft_itimer_is_running(t)` | Returns the volatile `running` flag. |
| `tbft_itimer_free(t)` | Stop and delete the underlying handle. |

`tbft_itimer_init` requests `dispatch_method = ESP_TIMER_TASK`
(`src/tbft_itimer.c:23-29`), so callbacks run on the dedicated `esp_timer`
task, not in an ISR. This means the callbacks can safely use FreeRTOS
APIs like `xEventGroupSetBits`.

The dispatcher at `src/tbft_itimer.c:6-13` clears `t->running` *before*
invoking the user callback. This ordering is what makes the
"`esp_timer_stop` then `esp_timer_start_once`" pattern in
`tbft_itimer_start` race-free: a callback in flight cannot resurrect the
flag between the clear and the start.

## Four timers in replica: vtimer, stimer, rtimer, ntimer

The replica struct declares four `tbft_itimer_t` slots at
`src/tbft_replica.h:101-104`:

```c
    /* Timers */
    tbft_itimer_t vtimer;  /* view-change timeout */
    tbft_itimer_t stimer;  /* status broadcast */
    /* rtimer (recovery) and ntimer (keep-alive) reserved for future use */
```

| Slot | Role | Initialised? |
|------|------|--------------|
| `vtimer` | One-shot: fires when the cluster has gone too long without progress; triggers `tbft_replica_send_view_change` | Yes (`src/tbft_replica.c:209-217`) |
| `stimer` | One-shot: fires periodically to broadcast a Status message | Yes (`src/tbft_replica.c:209-217`) |
| `rtimer` | Reserved for future recovery timing | No — comment in `tbft_replica_init` at `src/tbft_replica.c:206-208` notes that unused `esp_timer` handles are intentionally not allocated |
| `ntimer` | Reserved for future keep-alive | No |

`tbft_replica_free` (`src/tbft_replica.c:235-247`) only frees the two
allocated timers. The "not initialised" comment on lines 224 and 240
documents this intent.

## Event group decoupling (signal-only callbacks)

The replica owns an `EventGroupHandle_t` created in
`tbft_replica_init` at `src/tbft_replica.c:219-228`. The two timer
callbacks are pure setters:

```c
static void vtimer_cb(void *arg)        // src/tbft_replica.c:86-92
{
    tbft_replica_t *r = (tbft_replica_t *)arg;
    if (r->evt_group) {
        xEventGroupSetBits(r->evt_group, TBFT_EVT_VTIMER);
    }
}

static void stimer_cb(void *arg)        // src/tbft_replica.c:94-100
{
    tbft_replica_t *r = (tbft_replica_t *)arg;
    if (r->evt_group) {
        xEventGroupSetBits(r->evt_group, TBFT_EVT_STIMER);
    }
}
```

The bit constants are defined at `src/tbft_replica.h:152-153`:

```c
#define TBFT_EVT_VTIMER (1 << 0)
#define TBFT_EVT_STIMER (1 << 1)
```

Each callback returns immediately after a single `xEventGroupSetBits`
call. The callbacks do not touch the replica state, do not call any
cryptographic primitive, and do not call `tbft_node_send`. The cost is
bounded by the FreeRTOS event-group implementation — a few microseconds.

## Replica loop processing (tbft_replica_run checks event bits)

The main loop is `tbft_replica_run` at `src/tbft_replica.c:277`. The
event-group consumption lives at `src/tbft_replica.c:399-449`:

```c
EventBits_t bits = xEventGroupWaitBits(
    r->evt_group,
    TBFT_EVT_VTIMER | TBFT_EVT_STIMER,
    pdTRUE,   /* clear on exit */
    pdFALSE,  /* wait for any bit */
    pdMS_TO_TICKS(10));
```

On `TBFT_EVT_VTIMER`:

1. The code first checks `keys_ok >= threshold - 1`. If not enough
   session keys are fresh, the vtimer is *re-armed* (or stopped if no
   pending work) instead of triggering a view change — without keys,
   Prepare/Commit messages fail HMAC verification and a view change
   would be triggered spuriously (`src/tbft_replica.c:405-430`).
2. Otherwise, `tbft_replica_send_view_change(r)` runs in the replica
   task context. RSA signing of the new view-change message executes
   here, not in the callback.

On `TBFT_EVT_STIMER`:

1. Build a `tbft_status_rep_t` in `r->out_buf` (`src/tbft_replica.c:432-446`).
2. Send to `TBFT_ALL_REPLICAS`.
3. Re-arm the one-shot with `r->stimer_period_us` (`src/tbft_replica.c:448`).

The 10-ms `xEventGroupWaitBits` timeout acts as a periodic wakeup for
the run loop, so even without a timer firing the loop polls for
incoming messages, runs the dead-primary detector
(`src/tbft_replica.c:386-397`), and processes the gap-fill logic
(`src/tbft_replica.c:503-653`).

## Timer period configuration (Byz_init_replica)

`tbft_replica_init` initialises the periods to the Kconfig defaults
(`src/tbft_replica.c:200-203`):

```c
r->vtimer_period_us = TBFT_VIEW_CHANGE_TIMEOUT_US;
r->stimer_period_us = TBFT_STATUS_TIMEOUT_US;
```

The libbyz shim `Byz_init_replica` (in `src/tbft_libbyz.c`) overrides
these values from the parsed configuration file before starting the
timers. The timers themselves are *not* started in
`tbft_replica_init` — the comment at `src/tbft_replica.c:205-208` makes
this explicit:

```c
/* Init timers (not started — caller must set periods and start).
 * NOTE: rtimer (recovery) and ntimer (keep-alive) are reserved for
 * future use. They are not initialised or freed to avoid allocating
 * unused esp_timer handles. */
```

Starting happens later in the run loop: the vtimer is started on
demand (e.g. `src/tbft_replica.c:855` when a backup forwards a request)
and the stimer is re-armed after every fire.

## Why no heavy work in callbacks (RSA would block WiFi task)

`esp_timer` callbacks (with `ESP_TIMER_TASK` dispatch) execute on the
`esp_timer` task, a high-priority system task that also services other
component timers including the WiFi stack's internal timers. A long
callback would starve the WiFi task, causing:

- Beacon loss on the AP interface
- ESP-NOW send/recv queue stalls
- DHCP / ARP / TCP retransmit storms

RSA-2048 signing of a single message takes hundreds of milliseconds on
the ESP32-C3's crypto accelerator — orders of magnitude longer than
any reasonable timer-callback budget. By moving the signing into the
replica task, the WiFi task and other protocol timers continue to make
progress while the replica processes a view change.

The same argument applies to HMAC, but HMAC is fast enough (microseconds)
that a future change could move it back into the callback if profiling
showed the event-group hop was a bottleneck. The current architecture
treats event-group signalling as the cheaper direction of the
optimisation: the timer task sets a bit in O(1), the replica task
performs the work at its own priority, and other FreeRTOS tasks see
predictable scheduling.
